text: Why would a free man sail home, to a prison?
sub: Why would a free man sail home to a prison?

text: Oregon. Sohan Singh Bhukna, a farmer from Punjab, stacks lumber in a sawmill.
sub: Oregon. Sohan Singh Bhakna, a farmer from Punjab, stacks lumber in a sawmill.
asr: Oregon, Sohansingbukner, a farmer from Punjab, stacks lumber in a sawmill.

text: Here, he is taunted as a man from a slave country. The insult becomes his fuel.
sub: Here he is taunted as a man from a slave country. The insult becomes his fuel.

text: In nineteen thirteen, the workers found the Guddar Party, and choose him as its first president.
sub: In 1913 the workers found the Ghadar Party, and choose him as its first president.
asr: In 1913, the workers found the Gudhar Party and choose him as its first president.

text: He bows to no idol. As a Sikh, he bows only to the Guru's word: stand against tyranny.
sub: He bows to no idol. As a Sikh, he bows only to the Guru's word: stand against tyranny.

text: A saint, Baba Kayser Singh, had taught him to live for others.
sub: A saint, Baba Kesar Singh, had taught him to live for others.
asr: A saint, Boba-Kaser Singh, had taught him to live for others.

text: So in nineteen fourteen, as war begins, he sails for India, to raise a revolt.
sub: So in 1914, as war begins, he sails for India to raise a revolt.
asr: So in 1914, as war begins, he sails for India to raise a revolt.

text: The British are waiting. He is arrested as his ship reaches Calcutta.
sub: The British are waiting. He is arrested as his ship reaches Calcutta.

text: Sentenced to death, then to life, he spends sixteen years in prison.
sub: Sentenced to death, then to life, he spends 16 years in prison.
asr: Sentenced to death, then to life, he spent 16 years in prison.

text: He never bows. And he lives to see India free.
sub: He never bows. And he lives to see India free.
